title: Goal Thermostat - weekly check (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose:
Quick weekly scratchpad for my personal KPI "thermostat" — keep a small set of leading signals in range so I can nudge behavior rather than panic at the end of the quarter. Use this as the single source to copy from into 1:1s, manager updates, and sprint focus notes.

Context (why this matters):
- Quarterly objective: Improve platform stability and predictable latency while reducing per-token cost for customer workloads. My personal contribution needs to be measurable and small enough to act on weekly.
- Thermostat idea: keep two leading metrics in a narrow band; if one drifts, run a micro-experiment to bring it back.

Leading metrics I'm tracking this sprint (week ending 2025-03-07):
1) Regression rate on canary model (errors / 1k requests): 2.1 (target 0.8 - 1.2) — trending up compared to last week (1.6).
2) Median tail latency (p95) for small-gen routes (ms): 210ms (target 150 - 200) — slightly above target.
3) Personal throughput: number of ticket-hours I blocked and unblocked for SLO work: 6h (target 8h).

Quick hypothesis for the drift:
- Regression increase likely from new kernel selection logic merged last week that changes fallback ordering for quantized models. Small change but interacts with a subset of embeddings-heavy requests.
- Tail latency may be due to batching policy changes that increased contention during burst windows (see notes on presto-batcher test).

Experiments and micro-actions (this week):
- A: Revert fallback order for two affected models in canary and run 24h canary. Ticket: RED-482. Status: rolled back on canary; monitoring windows open. (Action owner: me)
- B: Add adaptive-batch cap for small-gen routes during peak minutes (00-10, 30-40 past the hour) — prototype in dev cluster. Status: PoC running, results noisier than expected.
- C: Quick audit of kernel selection logs (grep + small parser) to surface frequency of compatibility fallbacks in last 72h. Status: parsing script done; need approval to run cluster-wide.

What I learned / notes to self:
- Small config changes have outsized tail effects for minority workloads — need better tagging of 'risky' routes in rollout UX.
- Observability gap: we don't have an easy join between request fingerprint -> kernel path chosen -> fallback reason. Prioritize an event id that flows across subsystems.
- Timeboxing: when I find a regression, do a 2-hour deep-dive and then stop — otherwise I get sucked into debugging and deprioritize planned experiments.

Blockers and open questions:
- Need SRE support to run the cluster-wide kernel-log audit. Who on SRE is available this week? @Amina noted limited cycles.
- Can we add a lightweight flag to the rollout UI to pin fallback ordering for a canary cohort? If product/console team says no, I need to script it.
- Is the batching change responsible or a red herring? Our current experiment didn't isolate variables cleanly.

Decisions to make next check-in (by 2025-03-14):
- If canary rollback doesn't reduce regression rate to <1.5 by Wednesday, escalate to full rollback across dedicated pools.
- If p95 remains >200ms after adaptive-batch cap tweak and tuning, open an action to revert batching policy for the small-gen routes and run A/B for 48h.

Mini retrospective (last 2 weeks):
- Wins: shipped a small parser to index kernel selection logs; landed canary rollback quickly; documented the fallout path and informed support.
- Misses: I under-allocated time for researcher handoff on the batching PoC — friction caused rework. Need to schedule a 30-minute handoff with the batching author earlier.

Weekly micro-OKRs (3 items, measurable):
1) Reduce canary regression rate to <=1.2 by next check-in (metric: errors / 1k requests).
2) Get p95 for small-gen routes under 190ms (metric: p95 ms measured across last 24h).
3) Block/unblock >= 8 ticket-hours on SLO incidents and operational improvements (metric: my logged time in Clockify notes).

Tactical checklist (today / next 48h):
- [ ] Follow up with SRE to schedule kernel-log audit (include runbook + scope). Linked ticket: RED-499.
- [ ] Tune adaptive-batch cap parameters (alpha=0.6 -> 0.5) and redeploy PoC. Record results in /tmp/batch-experiments.csv.
- [ ] Draft a short note for the Console team requesting a 'pin fallback order' small UI affordance (1 paragraph, include link to example).
- [ ] Update my 1:1 note with manager: summary + ETA for rollback decision.

Notes to copy into 1:1 / manager update (2–3 lines):
- "Canary regression increased after kernel-selection tweak; rolled back on canary and monitoring is in flight. Working an adaptive batching PoC for small-gen routes — will revert batching if p95 doesn't improve after tuning."

Random scratch ideas (brainstorm / low fidelity):
- Thermostat automation: if one leading metric drifts by >25% for 2 consecutive checks, auto-create a tiny 'stabilize' workflow (templated checklist + owner + 24h deadline). Could be an action in the Console.
- Quick win: surface the last 3 rollout changes that touched a route directly on the route detail page (helps triage).

End note / meta: keep this intentionally messy. The point is speed > polish for weekly checks. Save a copy of the 'thermostat' results in the quarterly folder if we have a meaningful change to report.
